full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Choudhury J: These are the two appeals by leave from the judgment of the High Court Division in FMA Nos. 60 and 112 of 1995, one counter to the other. By the impugned judgment the High Court Division set aside the award made by the Subordinate Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka, on 23 February 1995 in Arbitration Case No. 38 of 1992 brought by the appellant and dismissed the arbitration case. 

 2. Briefly stated, the facts are these : in order to build the Kurmitola International Airport in Dhaka the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka initiated LA Case No. 110 of 1965 respecting 46.92 acres of land of Mouza Faydabad including the disputed plot Nos. 1311, 1312, 1313, 1314, 1315, 1323, 1328, 1330, 1345, 1362 and 1366 (measuring 6.97 acres). Notice under section 3 of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948, hereinafter called the Act, was issued on 13 June 1967. The Requisitioning authority took over possession of the land on 20-6-1967, 2-8-1967 and 1-9-1967. Meanwhile, notices under section 5(1) of the Act were duly issued signifying the intention of the Government to acquire the lands for the said purpose and the owners of the plots involved were paid initial compensation. 

 5. Upon the said application the Additional Land Acquisition Officer started Misc. Case No. 4 of 1979. He signed notices for service upon the persons who had already received provisional compensation and in whose presence the matter was necessary to be heard ad disposed of. These notices appear to have been served upon 27 out of 31 persons concerned till 26-2-1980 when the Additional Land Acquisition Officer heard the matter ex parte. He observed: 

 "It is found that Umed Ali and Yousuf are recorded purchasers of CS Plot No. 1266, 1345 and 1362 of Mouza Faidabad as in the CS parcha No. 182 but heirs of the CS recorded tenants and others have received payment of advance compensation money in suppression of the facts that these plots were already purchased by umed Ali and Yousuf. The petr MA Majid Dharaia who is a purchaser under regd deed No. 28034, 44714, 44718 dt. 28-11-79,deed No. 22712 dt. 31-10-78 and deed No. 37464 dt. 3-10-79 from the heirs of Umed Ali and Yousuf (Faraj enclosed). The petitioner filed petition claiming payment of compensation money of miscellaneous plots. This is a simple case of wrong payment to the following persons. 

 12. The Government and the appellant preferred FMA No. 112 of 1995 and FMA No. 60 of 1995 respectively. The High Court Division called for the records of the RA Case for examination and doubted the genuineness of the proceeding of assessment of compensation in favour of the appellant but ultimately set aside the award made by the Arbitrator on the ground that the appellant who was fully aware of the assessment of the compensation did not make his application under clause (aaa) of section 7 to the Arbitrator in time. Accordingly, FMA No. 60 of 1995 was dismissed and FMA No. 112 of 1995 was allowed by the impugned judgment dated 14 August 1996. 

 19. Then again, the claim of the appellant was heard and decided in his favour in Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1979 before any notice could be served upon the necessary persons although notices appear to have been gained and ordered to be served by 12 January 1980 positively. Strangely enough, the miscellaneous case was heard ex parte on 26 February 1980 and an order was passed by the Additional Land Acquisition Officer directing the persons who had drawn advance compensation money to refund the same. After a lengthy surmise without examining the necessary materials he further ordered that "award" be prepared in the name of the appellant in respect of the plots in question. 

 20. It is not understandable from the order in what manner the Additional Land Acquisition Officer had traced the title of the appellant and came to his conclusion. The appellant as seen above, had already drawn Taka 4,46,200.00 i.e. almost the entire amount towards the compensation till 1 December 1984. After finalization of the proceeding for acquisition and notification thereof in the Gazette the Additional Land Acquisition Officer was required to obtain the approval of the Government before issuing the notice of the assessment of the compensation in Form j under clause (aa) of section 7. But the records show that no step for obtaining the approval of the Government was taken in the case of appellant. 

 23. The sequence of events described here above would show that the appellant made application before the Additional Land Acquisition Officer claiming compensation when he had no title or interest in the case lands. He came to the scene only in 1979, 12 years after the notices under section 5(1) and 5(3) of Act were served. The manner in which his case was processed naturally leads one to believe that there was unfairness and collusion in the entire deal. Also the notice of the assessment on the appellant in Form J was without any legal authority and obviously, it was collusively procured. This notice cannot be considered a notice under clause (aa) of section 7 of the Act. Such a notice could not entitle the appellant to file the arbitration case. The arbitration proceeding was, therefore, without jurisdiction.
